claims.claim: Verapamil, a structurally related dimethoxyphenyl tertiary amine with the highest transfer likelihood to the query, has absolute oral bioavailability of 52 ± 13% and 52.3% in cirrhosis patients, well above the 20% threshold.
Valbenazine, which shares a dimethoxy-substituted fused bicyclic core and a basic tertiary amine side chain, has absolute oral bioavailability of approximately 49% in humans.
Encainide, another basic dimethoxyphenyl drug, has mean oral bioavailability of 42% (range 7–82%) and 41.9% in separate studies, supporting F ≥ 20%.
Noscapine, a poly-methoxylated alkaloid, has oral bioavailability of about 30% in humans, above the threshold.
